transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’ve been having thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes driving home, I wonder if my family and my students would be better off without me. It scares me, because I don’t want to do anything to myself.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I just know I’ve been struggling and feeling overwhelmed.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah. I used to look forward to softball, book club, working in my garden, even the robotics club at school. Now I mostly just go through the motions, or I cancel because none of it really feels enjoyable anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About a year and seven months, I think. It started when I took on the STEM assessment redesign along with my regular teaching load.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt unusually energized, elated, or wired, and needed much less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. I can’t remember having a time where I felt unusually energized or needed a lot less sleep.
Before this started a year and a half ago, have you ever experienced another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest like this?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time like this before.
How has your sleep been over this past year and a half?

It’s been pretty bad. I’ll be exhausted, but then I just lie awake replaying assessment deadlines or things I think I got wrong in class. And I often wake up around four in the morning and can’t really get back to sleep.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over this time?
Yeah. On most school days I kind of forget to eat, or just avoid it until late afternoon. My clothes have gotten noticeably looser over the past year, even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy nearly every day?
Yes. By the time I get through teaching and a department meeting, my body feels so heavy. Even making dinner or answering a few parent emails feels like climbing a hill.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, thinking clearly, or making everyday decisions?

Yes. I’ll read the same student response three or four times and still can’t work out what score to give it. Even simple things, like deciding which lab supplies to order, can leave me stuck for an hour.
